$comment: First-load transfer budget for the Cloudflare Pages SPA, enforced by
`npm run test:release-budget` against `dist/` after `npm run build`.
These are regression ratchets measured from a real build, not a claim that
the current numbers are good. Raising a number is a deliberate act and
belongs in the same commit as the change that needs it.
Gzip is used as the transfer-size proxy because Cloudflare Pages negotiates
brotli or gzip; brotli is smaller, so a gzip budget is the conservative one.
Enforced by `docs/release/probes/lighthouse-budget.mjs`, not by CI: it needs a
real Chrome and takes minutes.
The composite performance score is measured over three full passes on
2026-08-24 and moved by up to 20 points between them on the same build --
42-65 on emulated mobile for `/`, 81-99 on desktop for `/settings`. It is
therefore gated only at a catastrophic-regression floor, well under the worst
*best-of-runs* value observed. The precise performance ratchet is the
deterministic first-load transfer budget above, which runs in CI.
Accessibility (100 in all 36 measurements), best practices and CLS were stable
across the same three passes, so those are gated close to what was measured.
Each combination is run `RUNS` times (default 2). Scores take the best run and
Each combination is run `RUNS` times (default 2). Performance, LCP and CLS take
the BEST run; accessibility and best practices take the worst. Interference from
other work on the machine only ever degrades a Lighthouse result, and a genuine
layout shift is deterministic, so a CLS figure that appears on one run and not
the other is measurement, not the page. The worst CLS is still printed and
warned about so a real intermittent shift stays visible -- see the 0.186 episode
in docs/release/2026-08-24-release-gates.md.
Measured against a production-mode build of the offline demo (`VITE_LOCAL_MODE=1`)
served by `vite preview`, so no Supabase project is contacted and no private
data is involved.
